F23-CHCL-PWD.supplierNote: Major, very recent trade action: the EU adopted anti-dumping duties of 90.0% to 115.9% on choline chloride imports from China, published December 19, 2025 and effective for five years — Balchem and Eastman (the two named EU producers) publicly welcomed the decision as protecting the EU feed/food supply chain from 'unfair trade practices.' This is a real, executed policy change that will materially raise the cost of Chinese-origin choline chloride for any EU buyer, not a proposal under discussion. BASF's production capacity has shrunk significantly over time (from plants in Germany, Brazil, Mexico, and Thailand down to a small ~15KT German-only operation), consistent with broader industry consolidation toward Balchem/Eastman/DSM-Firmenich as the remaining Western majors.

compliance.flag: EU anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports (90.0-115.9%, effective Dec 19 2025)
compliance.name: Major, already-executed trade policy change
compliance.desc: Any EU buyer currently sourcing choline chloride from China faces a duty increase of 90-116% effective immediately for a 5-year term — this is not a risk to monitor, it is already in effect and should be reflected in any current EU sourcing cost comparison.

compliance.flag: Dual food/feed and industrial (oilfield) grade specification
compliance.name: Distinct grades, not interchangeable
compliance.desc: Feed-grade choline chloride requires nutritional/purity certification distinct from industrial oilfield grade — confirm the certified grade matches the intended end use.

macroDrivers.title: Global poultry and swine production growth is the core structural demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As the highest-volume feed additive globally, choline chloride demand tracks global animal protein production growth directly and durably — a low-margin but very large-volume commodity underpinning essentially the entire feed premix industry.

substitution.title: Betaine as a partial methyl-donor substitute in some feed formulations
substitution.body: Betaine can substitute for choline in some specific nutritional roles (methyl donor function) but does not replace choline's broader essential-nutrient functions — a partial, formulation-specific substitution option only.

functionalities.name: Most widely used skin/hair vitamin active globally
functionalities.desc: Provitamin B5 (D-panthenol) is converted to pantothenic acid on the skin, providing moisturizing and wound-healing benefits — present in a very large share of shampoos, conditioners, and moisturizers worldwide, making it one of the highest-volume single cosmetic actives by usage frequency, if not by tonnage.

functionalities.name: Shares upstream chemistry with feed-grade Vitamin B5
functionalities.desc: Produced via the same core synthesis route as feed-grade calcium pantothenate, then reduced to the alcohol form — the cosmetic-grade product commands a materially higher margin for the same core chemistry, reflecting purity and application requirements rather than a fundamentally different production process.

items: Moisturizing and conditioning active in shampoo, conditioner, and skin moisturizer formulations — present in a very large share of personal care products globally

F23-DPAN-LIQ.supplierNote: D-panthenol follows the same DSM-Firmenich/BASF-plus-Chinese-bulk-producer pattern seen across the vitamin cluster in this library (see the F23 vitamin batch), with Daicel a notable additional Japanese specialty producer. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Cosmetic-grade purity certification
compliance.name: Grade-specific requirement, distinct from feed grade
compliance.desc: Cosmetic-grade D-panthenol requires purity and stability documentation distinct from feed-grade calcium pantothenate — confirm certification matches the intended personal-care application.

macroDrivers.title: Structural growth in 'skinification' of hair care and daily moisturizer use
macroDrivers.body: The ongoing consumer trend toward skincare-grade actives in hair care products, plus generally rising daily moisturizer/skincare routine adoption globally, is a durable structural demand driver for this ingredient beyond any single product category cycle.

substitution.title: Plant-derived panthenol alternatives (niche, emerging)
substitution.body: Some formulators are exploring biotechnology or plant-extraction routes to panthenol for 'natural origin' claims, but these remain niche relative to the established synthetic route — not yet a meaningful supply-side substitution factor.

functionalities.name: Universal fragrance carrier solvent
functionalities.desc: The standard carrier/diluent solvent for fragrance concentrates, typically present at 30-60% by weight of every finished fragrance compound — an almost invisible but essentially universal component of the fragrance supply chain.

functionalities.name: Co-product of propylene glycol manufacture
functionalities.desc: Produced as the higher-molecular-weight fraction separated by distillation during propylene glycol production — this product's cost structure and supplier base essentially mirror this library's existing propylene glycol (SOL-MPG-LIQ) model, just with different distillation-cut economics.

items: Universal carrier/diluent solvent for fragrance concentrates — present in the large majority of finished perfume and fragrance compounds
Humectant in personal care formulations

tags: Augeo brand — post-demerger oxygenated solvents business, European production base

SOL-DPG-LIQ.supplierNote: DPG (dipropylene glycol) is a propylene-oxide co-product (see BCI-PO-LIQ, SOL-MPG-LIQ) valued specifically as a low-odor fragrance/personal-care carrier solvent. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Fragrance-grade low-odor/low-aldehyde specification
compliance.name: Grade-specific requirement, not a general compliance issue
compliance.desc: Fragrance-grade DPG requires tighter odor and aldehyde-content specifications than industrial grade, since any off-note would compromise the fragrance compound it carries — confirm grade before comparing supplier pricing.

macroDrivers.title: Fragrance industry volume growth is a direct, linear demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Because DPG is present at high weight-percentage in nearly every fragrance compound, its demand tracks overall fine fragrance and functional-fragrance (household/personal care) volume growth almost directly — a genuinely reliable structural demand link rather than an indirect proxy.

substitution.title: Isopropyl myristate and other ester carriers (niche, formulation-specific)
substitution.body: Some fragrance formulations use alternative carrier solvents for specific solubility or sensory requirements, but DPG's cost-effectiveness and broad compatibility keep it the default choice for the large majority of fragrance compounds — a real but limited substitution dynamic.

functionalities.name: Most widely used UVB absorber globally
functionalities.desc: The single most common UVB-absorbing organic UV filter in commercial sunscreens worldwide via simple esterification of p-methoxycinnamic acid with 2-ethylhexanol — extremely high-volume despite facing more active regulatory scrutiny than most other filters in this category.

functionalities.name: Subject to the most geographically fragmented regulatory landscape of any UV filter here
functionalities.desc: Banned outright in Hawaii and Palau specifically to protect coral reefs, while remaining fully approved and dominant in most other markets — creating genuinely different formulation requirements by destination market, not just a uniform global compliance question.

items: Primary UVB absorber in sunscreen and daily-SPF formulations — the highest-volume organic UV filter globally

tags: Brand owner/specifier — Parsol MCX heritage brand; does not operate own OMC synthesis. Sources from BASF and generic producers
Confirmed integrated UV-filter producer — Uvinul brand, Grenzach-Wyhlen (DE) production site

F10-OMC-LIQ.supplierNote: Octinoxate (ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate) shares the same DSM-Firmenich/BASF-plus-Chinese-generic pattern as avobenzone (see F21-AVOB-PWD) — it is facing growing regulatory scrutiny in some markets (e.g. Hawaii and Palau reef-safety bans) that is reshaping regional demand. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Hawaii/Palau bans (executed)
compliance.name: Real, in-effect market-access restriction
compliance.desc: Octinoxate is banned for sale in Hawaii and Palau specifically to protect coral reef ecosystems — an already-executed market restriction requiring destination-specific formulation, not a pending review.

compliance.flag: EU Commission opinion finalized 2025 — endocrine-active but approved ≤10%
compliance.name: Review resolved, not still pending
compliance.desc: Correction to an earlier characterization of this as an open review: the European Commission finalized its opinion on octinoxate in 2025, concluding it is an endocrine-active substance but remains safe for use as a UV filter at concentrations up to 10% — current EU approval status is confirmed and settled, not pending.

macroDrivers.title: Reef-safe formulation trend adds a genuine bifurcation to the market
macroDrivers.body: Growing 'reef-safe' marketing and destination-specific regulation (Hawaii, Palau, parts of Mexico) is structurally splitting sunscreen formulation strategy by geography — a durable trend requiring dual-formulation capability for global brands.

substitution.title: Amiloxate (isoamyl p-methoxycinnamate)
substitution.body: A close structural analog marketed as an alternative cinnamate-type UVB absorber, used in some formulations but without octinoxate's scale or regulatory track record — a real but minor substitution option.

functionalities.name: SPF-boosting UVB absorber
functionalities.desc: Esterification of salicylic acid with homomenthol (via an isophorone intermediate derived from acetone) — valued specifically for boosting the SPF performance of a formulation beyond what its individual filters would suggest, present in most US sunscreen formulas.

functionalities.name: Facing active 'clean beauty' consumer pressure despite regulatory approval
functionalities.desc: A 2023 US consumer survey found 68% of respondents prioritize avoiding homosalate even where it remains fully permitted — a genuine reputational/demand risk distinct from any actual regulatory restriction.

items: SPF-enhancing UVB absorber, especially prevalent in US sunscreen formulations

tags: Brand owner/specifier — Parsol HMS heritage brand; does not operate own HMS synthesis. Sources from contract manufacturers and generic producers
Confirmed integrated UV-filter producer — Grenzach-Wyhlen (DE) production site

F10-HMS-LIQ.supplierNote: Homosalate follows the same UV-filter producer pattern as the rest of this cluster — DSM-Firmenich/BASF branded product plus a growing generic Chinese supply base. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: EU SCCS Group A review (ongoing since 2019)
compliance.name: Active review, current approval unaffected
compliance.desc: Homosalate remains part of an ongoing EU safety data review alongside three other UV filters — no restriction currently in effect, but this is a live regulatory topic to monitor, not a settled matter.

macroDrivers.title: US sunscreen formulation dependency is a structural demand anchor
macroDrivers.body: Homosalate's SPF-boosting role makes it near-essential to many US-market sunscreen formulations meeting FDA SPF testing requirements — a durable structural demand base even amid consumer sentiment headwinds.

substitution.title: Alternative SPF-boosting esters (polyester-8 class)
substitution.body: Similar to octocrylene, newer non-active SPF-boosting esters are emerging, but homosalate's specific salicylate chemistry and cost profile keep it the incumbent choice for most current formulations.

functionalities.name: High-efficiency UVB absorber at very low use levels
functionalities.desc: Triazine ring chemistry with triple substitution achieves high SPF contribution at concentrations far below other organic filters — an attractive eco-profile that appeals to formulators targeting minimal total filter loading.

functionalities.name: Most synthetically complex UV filter in this category
functionalities.desc: Requires coupling cyanuric chloride (itself from urea + chlorine) with 2-ethylhexanol and p-aminobenzoic acid across multiple substitution steps — genuinely more complex chemistry than the simple esterifications used for salicylate/cinnamate filters, reflected in its higher margin.

items: High-efficiency UVB absorber for low-filter-load, high-eco-class sunscreen formulations

tags: Brand originator — Parsol EHT; more specialized/patent-protected molecule where DSM-Firmenich retains stronger supply-chain control than for the older off-patent UV filters

F10-EHT-PWD.supplierNote: Ethylhexyl triazone is a newer-generation, more chemically complex UV filter than avobenzone/octinoxate/homosalate — this is a confirmed narrow market: only DSM-Firmenich (originator, Parsol EHT) and BASF (Uvinul T 150) are established, verifiable producers at commercial scale, with the more complex synthesis and continuing specialty positioning keeping it from broadly genericizing the way older UV filters have. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Low use-level formulation requirement
compliance.name: Formulation-specific, not a compliance risk
compliance.desc: Regulatory maximum use concentrations for ethylhexyl triazone are lower than most other UV filters (around 5%) — a formulation design constraint rather than a safety restriction.

compliance.flag: Not part of the US FDA OTC sunscreen monograph
compliance.name: Approved in the EU/Japan but not usable in US sunscreen products
compliance.desc: Ethylhexyl triazone is approved as a UV filter in the EU, Japan, and other markets, but is not included in the US FDA's OTC sunscreen monograph — a genuine, structural market-access limitation for US-facing sunscreen formulations specifically, distinct from its EU/international regulatory status.

macroDrivers.title: Eco-formulation and minimal-filter-load trend favors this chemistry specifically
macroDrivers.body: Brands targeting genuinely minimal total UV filter loading (for sensory or environmental positioning) have a structural reason to favor this filter's high per-unit efficiency — a differentiated, durable niche versus commodity UV filter demand.

substitution.title: Bis-ethylhexyloxyphenol methoxyphenyl triazine (PARSOL Shield)
substitution.body: Another DSM-Firmenich triazine-family broad-spectrum filter competes for some of the same high-efficiency, low-load formulation space — an internal product-line substitution more than an external competitive threat.

functionalities.name: Provitamin A source and natural-orange pigment
functionalities.desc: Synthetic beta-carotene serves a dual role: a provitamin A nutrient source and a natural-orange pigmentation agent in poultry and aquaculture feed — via Wittig reaction coupling beta-ionone (C13) with a C15 triphenylphosphonium salt.

functionalities.name: Directly exposed to the same isophytol supply chain as Vitamin A and Vitamin E
functionalities.desc: Shares upstream terpene chemistry with vitamin A/E production at the major producers — meaning a disruption at one producer's isophytol/citral facility can simultaneously affect vitamin A, vitamin E, and carotenoid supply, as demonstrated in 2024.

items: Provitamin A source and orange pigmentation in poultry and aquaculture feed
Natural-appearing orange food colorant
Antioxidant and colorant in cosmetic formulations

F23-BCAR-PWD.supplierNote: Beta-carotene production splits between synthetic routes (dominated by DSM-Firmenich and BASF) and natural/fermentation or algae-derived routes (LycoRed and others) — the same DSM/BASF/China triad seen across the vitamin category applies here as well. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: BASF force majeure event (2024), now resolved
compliance.name: Historical supply disruption, useful context for supplier risk assessment
compliance.desc: The 2024 BASF Ludwigshafen fire is a concrete, real example of single-site concentration risk in this category — even though normalized by end of 2025, it's a legitimate data point for any multi-year single-source contract risk discussion.

macroDrivers.title: Poultry and aquaculture feed volume growth is the core structural demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As a functional pigment plus provitamin A source, demand tracks global poultry and aquaculture production growth directly.

substitution.title: Natural beta-carotene (algae/fungal fermentation route)
substitution.body: Blakeslea trispora fermentation and Dunaliella algae extraction are commercially viable natural alternatives, generally at a cost premium — a real substitution path for natural-positioned feed/food brands, distinct from the synthetic route's cost structure.

functionalities.name: Essential for commercial salmon/trout pink flesh color
functionalities.desc: Without astaxanthin supplementation, farmed salmon and trout flesh is naturally grey — this is not a cosmetic nicety but a commercial necessity, since consumers expect and pay a premium for the characteristic pink color; the highest-value feed additive in this library by unit cost.

functionalities.name: Highest-share single carotenoid in the feed carotenoids market
functionalities.desc: Astaxanthin holds roughly 32% of the global feed carotenoids market by revenue, ahead of beta-carotene, canthaxanthin, and lutein — reflecting the salmon/aquaculture industry's willingness to pay a premium for reliable, consistent pigmentation.

items: Essential pink pigmentation additive in salmon and trout aquaculture feed — without it, farmed fish flesh remains grey

tags: Major synthetic astaxanthin producer for aquaculture
Asia challenger — leading natural (Haematococcus algae) astaxanthin producer
China Asia challenger — natural astaxanthin producer
Natural astaxanthin from Hawaiian algae cultivation

F23-ASTA-PWD.supplierNote: Astaxanthin has a distinctive dual-route market: DSM-Firmenich and BASF dominate the synthetic route used heavily in salmon/aquaculture feed, while natural astaxanthin (from Haematococcus pluvialis algae) is a separate, higher-value specialty segment led by Japanese (Fuji Chemical/AstaReal), Chinese (Yunnan Alphy), Icelandic (Algalif), and US (Cyanotech) producers serving the human-nutrition/nutraceutical market. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Synthetic vs. natural sourcing distinction, EU labeling relevance
compliance.name: Genuine market segmentation, not a regulatory restriction
compliance.desc: European aquaculture increasingly specifies natural-sourced astaxanthin for premium/branded salmon programs — verify which sourcing route a quote covers, since synthetic and natural astaxanthin are not interchangeable for brands with natural-sourcing commitments even though both are approved.

macroDrivers.title: Global salmon and trout aquaculture growth is a direct, premium-linked demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Salmon processors tie bonus payments to fillet color/hue metrics, cementing steady, price-inelastic demand for astaxanthin even during general feed-cost inflation cycles — a genuinely durable demand anchor distinct from most other feed additives.

substitution.title: Canthaxanthin as a partial pigmentation substitute
substitution.body: Canthaxanthin can contribute red-orange pigmentation in some aquaculture applications but does not fully replicate astaxanthin's specific pink hue profile expected by salmon markets — a limited, not full, substitution option.

functionalities.name: Premium vitamin D3 metabolite bypassing hepatic hydroxylation
functionalities.desc: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3 is the metabolite the liver would normally produce from standard D3 — supplying it directly bypasses that hepatic conversion step, giving more reliable, consistent vitamin D activity especially valuable when liver function is compromised by heat stress or disease.

functionalities.name: Direct derivative of this library's existing feed-grade Vitamin D3 model
functionalities.desc: Produced via chemical or enzymatic hydroxylation of cholecalciferol (standard D3) — its cost structure is best understood as the existing D3 cost model plus a substantial hydroxylation/purification conversion premium, not a fundamentally different feedstock chain.

items: Premium vitamin D3 metabolite for poultry and swine feed — commands a 5-10x price premium over standard D3 for bypassing hepatic hydroxylation

tags: Category-defining branded product — 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 for improved bioavailability in poultry/swine feed
Asia challenger — vitamin D3 and derivative specialist

F23-HYD3-PWD.supplierNote: 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 (calcifediol) is a more specialized, higher-bioavailability derivative of standard vitamin D3 — DSM-Firmenich’s Rovimix Hy-D is the category-defining branded product with patent-protected positioning in much of the market, giving DSM a stronger relative position here than in the more commoditized standard-D3 market. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: EFSA authorization across all animal species (recently confirmed)
compliance.name: Regulatory tailwind, not a restriction
compliance.desc: EFSA has recently confirmed authorization of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 across all animal species, removing prior species-specific authorization gaps — a positive, expanding-use regulatory development.

macroDrivers.title: Heat-stress and disease-resilience nutrition programs are a growing structural driver
macroDrivers.body: As livestock heat-stress management becomes a bigger focus (climate-driven), Hy-D's advantage in maintaining vitamin D activity under compromised liver function conditions is an increasingly relevant, durable value proposition beyond routine premix inclusion.

substitution.title: Standard cholecalciferol (D3) at higher inclusion rates
substitution.body: For healthy animals without liver-function concerns, standard D3 at appropriate dosing remains a functional, much lower-cost alternative — Hy-D's premium is justified specifically by its bypass of hepatic conversion, not a universal requirement.

functionalities.name: Stabilized, water-soluble Vitamin K source for feed
functionalities.desc: Menadione (Vitamin K3) is oxidized from 2-methylnaphthalene then complexed with sodium bisulfite specifically for stability — the raw menadione itself is not stable enough for direct feed use, making this bisulfite complex the standard commercial form.

functionalities.name: Essential for blood coagulation and bone metabolism in poultry
functionalities.desc: Routinely included in poultry premixes to reduce hemorrhagic disorders and support calcium-binding proteins involved in bone mineralization — a small-dose but functionally essential feed component.

items: Vitamin K source in poultry and swine premixes — supports blood coagulation and bone metabolism

tags: China Asia challenger — 4th-largest global vitamin producer, citral-based cost/scale advantage

F23-VITK3-PWD.supplierNote: Vitamin K3 (menadione) follows the broader synthetic-vitamin pattern in this library: European majors (DSM-Firmenich, BASF) retain premium/branded positioning, but China now supplies the majority of global bulk vitamin active-ingredient capacity (Zhejiang NHU, Zhejiang Medicine, and others collectively supply 60-80% of global bulk vitamin capacity across the vitamin category). Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: FDA/regulatory traceability requirements for premix ingredients
compliance.name: Increasing documentation burden, industry-wide trend
compliance.desc: Regulators have expanded traceability requirements for feed premix ingredients — expect increased documentation/audit requests from suppliers as a standard part of qualification, not an unusual ask.

macroDrivers.title: Rising global meat protein consumption is the core structural demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Growing meat consumption in middle-income economies is directly increasing demand for fortified feed additives supporting livestock growth and reduced mortality — a durable, multi-year volume driver.

substitution.title: Menadione nicotinamide bisulfite (alternative stabilized form)
substitution.body: A related stabilized menadione complex used in some feed formulations as an alternative to the sodium bisulfite form — a minor formulation-level substitution, not a different underlying active ingredient.

functionalities.name: Essential B-vitamin via oxazole/Diels-Alder synthesis route
functionalities.desc: Produced via multi-step synthesis combining acrylonitrile, formaldehyde, and acetaldehyde-derived intermediates through oxazole ring chemistry — lower tonnage than most feed vitamins but high value per kilo.

functionalities.name: 81% of demand from animal nutrition specifically
functionalities.desc: Despite broad relevance to food/beverage and pharmaceutical uses, animal nutrition represents the large majority (81%) of Vitamin B6 sales volume — genuinely feed-market-dominated demand, not evenly split across end uses.

items: Essential B6 vitamin in poultry, swine, and other livestock premixes — animal nutrition represents ~81% of total market demand

F23-VITB6-PWD.supplierNote: Same broad producer pattern as other B-vitamins in this cluster — European majors hold premium/branded share, Chinese bulk producers (NHU, Zhejiang Medicine, Xinfa) supply the majority of global volume. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Feed-grade vs. pharmaceutical-grade specification
compliance.name: Distinct grades with real regulatory-documentation implications
compliance.desc: Pharmaceutical-grade pyridoxine HCl requires GMP production and formal drug master file documentation (e.g. DSM-Firmenich's active China DMF) — feed-grade material from commodity Chinese producers does not carry this documentation and cannot substitute for pharma applications.

macroDrivers.title: Animal nutrition demand dominance makes this a livestock-cycle-linked commodity, not a diversified vitamin
macroDrivers.body: With 81% of demand from animal nutrition specifically, Vitamin B6 pricing and demand track livestock production cycles more directly than more end-market-diversified vitamins in this library.

substitution.title: No significant functional substitute — genuine essential nutrient
substitution.body: Unlike most chemicals in this library, Vitamin B6 has no real substitution option for its core nutritional function — sourcing flexibility exists at the supplier level (China commodity vs. Western pharma-grade) but not at the molecule level.

functionalities.name: Most widely used synthetic emollient in personal care
functionalities.desc: Simple esterification of myristic acid (C14) with isopropanol gives a colorless, virtually odorless oil present in nearly every skin cream, lotion, and makeup product — the highest-volume single emollient by usage frequency in this category.

functionalities.name: Penetration enhancer function beyond simple emollience
functionalities.desc: Helps carry fat-soluble actives into skin, making it functionally important in pharmaceutical topical formulations as well as cosmetics — a dual cosmetic/pharma role.

items: Universal emollient in skin creams, lotions, and makeup — present in the large majority of formulations
Penetration enhancer for fat-soluble actives in topical pharmaceutical formulations
Pharmaceutical topical penetration enhancer in transdermal drug delivery systems

OLE-IPM-LIQ.supplierNote: Isopropyl myristate and the other emollient esters in this cluster (see OLE-CCT-LIQ, OLE-CEH-LIQ, OLE-DCC-LIQ, OLE-C1215AB-LIQ) share a very similar producer base of personal-care-focused ester specialists — Croda, BASF Care Creations, and the Southeast Asian oleochemical integrators (Emery, KLK OLEO) supplying the fatty-acid/fatty-alcohol feedstock used in esterification. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Coconut/palm kernel oil feedstock sustainability sourcing
compliance.name: Feedstock-level ESG consideration, not a restriction on the finished product
compliance.desc: RSPO or equivalent sustainable-sourcing certification for the underlying palm kernel oil is an increasingly common buyer requirement — verify certification chain if sustainability claims matter for the end formulation.

macroDrivers.title: Universal formulation-base status makes demand track total personal care volume directly
macroDrivers.body: As one of the most broadly used single emollients, IPM demand is less about category trends and more a direct function of overall skin care/cosmetics production volume growth.

substitution.title: Caprylic/capric triglyceride and other light esters
substitution.body: Formulators frequently substitute among several light emollient esters (IPM, CCT, cetyl ethylhexanoate) based on specific skin-feel requirements — genuine but performance-driven substitution, not a simple cost swap.

functionalities.name: Second most-used emollient after IPM
functionalities.desc: Valued specifically for its light skin feel and oxidative stability — esterification of glycerine with C8/C10 fatty acids from coconut oil fractionation gives a clear, colorless, highly stable oil.

functionalities.name: Genuine antioxidant stability advantage over many emollient esters
functionalities.desc: The medium-chain-triglyceride structure resists oxidation better than longer-chain esters, extending shelf life in finished formulations — a real, not marketing-only, technical differentiator.

items: Light-feel emollient in skin creams, lotions, and makeup with superior oxidative stability vs. longer-chain esters
MCT oil carrier in nutritional supplements, sports nutrition, and functional food products

tags: Asia challenger — coconut/palm-kernel-derived caprylic/capric feedstock proximity

OLE-CCT-LIQ.supplierNote: Same emollient-ester producer universe as isopropyl myristate (see OLE-IPM-LIQ) — caprylic/capric triglyceride is coconut/palm-kernel-oil-derived, giving Southeast Asian oleochemical producers a natural feedstock advantage. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Coconut/palm kernel oil feedstock sustainability sourcing
compliance.name: Same feedstock-level ESG consideration as IPM
compliance.desc: RSPO or equivalent certification relevant for sustainability-conscious buyers.

macroDrivers.title: Premium light-emollient positioning is a durable, function-driven demand segment
macroDrivers.body: CCT's oxidative stability advantage keeps it favored specifically for premium, longer-shelf-life formulations — a genuine functional niche rather than pure commodity substitution with IPM.

substitution.title: Isopropyl myristate and other light esters
substitution.body: Interchangeable with IPM and similar esters in many formulations based on specific sensory/stability requirements.

functionalities.name: The 'champagne of surfactants' — premium mild anionic
functionalities.desc: Two-step synthesis (coconut fatty acid esterified with sodium isethionate) gives an exceptionally mild, low-irritation anionic surfactant — the standard for premium syndet (synthetic detergent) bars and sulfate-free cleansers.

functionalities.name: Fastest-growing surfactant category tied to sulfate-free trend
functionalities.desc: Directly benefits from the structural, multi-year consumer shift away from SLS/SLES-based sulfate systems toward gentler cleansing technology — a durable, not cyclical, demand driver.

items: Primary mild anionic surfactant in syndet bars, sulfate-free shampoos, and premium facial cleansers

tags: Asia challenger — long history in isethionate chemistry via syndet bar heritage
Specialty personal-care ingredient distributor — does not operate own isethionate synthesis capacity

SUR-SCI-PWD.supplierNote: SCI (sodium cocoyl isethionate) is a premium, mild anionic surfactant historically associated with syndet bar soap (its "champagne of surfactants" reputation) — the producer base is more concentrated than commodity surfactants because the two-step esterification/isethionation process is more specialized. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Coconut oil sourcing, sustainability certification
compliance.name: Feedstock-level consideration
compliance.desc: Same RSPO/sustainable sourcing relevance as other coconut-derived personal care ingredients in this library.

macroDrivers.title: Sulfate-free reformulation is a structural, multi-year demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As brands continue reformulating away from SLS/SLES, SCI is one of the primary beneficiary mild-anionic replacements — a durable trend, not a short-term fad.

substitution.title: Sodium lauroyl sarcosinate and other mild anionics
substitution.body: Several other mild anionic surfactants compete for the same sulfate-free reformulation demand — genuine but performance/cost-driven substitution among a broader mild-anionic category.

functionalities.name: Most widely used ethoxylated sorbitan ester globally
functionalities.desc: Serves as emulsifier and solubilizer across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications simultaneously — genuinely universal, not category-specific.

functionalities.name: Critical pharmaceutical excipient role beyond personal care
functionalities.desc: Used in vaccine formulations and injectable drug products as a stabilizer — a distinct, higher-scrutiny grade tier exists specifically for pharma/vaccine use, separate from cosmetic-grade material.

items: Emulsifier and solubilizer across a very broad range of formulations
Emulsifier in ice cream, baked goods, and other food formulations
Pharmaceutical excipient, including vaccine and injectable formulation stabilization — a distinct, higher-purity grade

tags: Owns the Tween trademark; leading global polysorbate producer, pharma-grade capability
Asia challenger — established Japanese specialty surfactant producer
China Asia challenger — growing food/pharma-grade capacity

SUR-PS80-LIQ.supplierNote: Polysorbate 80 is used simultaneously across personal care, pharmaceutical (including as a vaccine excipient), and food applications, so pharma-grade production (subject to GMP/USP/EP compliance) is more concentrated among a few majors (Croda, Evonik, BASF) than the broader cosmetic-grade market, where Japanese and Chinese producers compete more directly on cost. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Pharma-grade vs. cosmetic/food-grade distinction
compliance.name: Real, consequential grade separation
compliance.desc: Pharmaceutical and vaccine-grade Polysorbate 80 requires substantially higher purity and documentation than cosmetic/food-grade material — do not substitute one for the other; this is a genuine safety-relevant distinction, not just a pricing tier.

macroDrivers.title: Vaccine/injectable pharmaceutical demand adds a distinct, less cyclical demand layer
macroDrivers.body: Beyond personal care and food, Polysorbate 80's pharmaceutical excipient role (including in mRNA vaccine formulations) provides a demand base less tied to consumer discretionary spending cycles.

substitution.title: Sorbitan monostearate (Span) and other sorbitan esters
substitution.body: Often used in combination with, rather than as a substitute for, Polysorbate 80 in classic Span/Tween emulsion systems — complementary more than competitive.

functionalities.name: Light emollient with excellent spreading properties
functionalities.desc: Esterification of cetyl alcohol (C16) with 2-ethylhexanoic acid gives a light, fast-spreading oil favored where a non-greasy skin feel is required.

functionalities.name: Shares upstream chemistry with several other emollients in this category
functionalities.desc: The 2-ethylhexanoic acid input traces to the same 2-EH/propylene chain used across octyldodecanol, dicaprylyl carbonate, and several UV filters in this library.

items: Light, fast-spreading emollient in skin and hair care formulations

OLE-CEH-LIQ.supplierNote: Same emollient-ester producer universe as OLE-IPM-LIQ — cetyl ethylhexanoate is a lighter-feel ester valued in premium skin-care formulations. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: No significant compliance or substitution concern identified
compliance.name: Standard personal-care emollient ester — no acute regulatory flag
compliance.desc: Built from a synthetic fatty alcohol and a petrochemical-derived acid rather than a directly-regulated commodity; no EUDR exposure and no known active substitution pressure beyond normal formulation competition among emollient esters.

macroDrivers.title: Light-feel formulation trend supports steady demand
macroDrivers.body: Consumer preference for non-greasy, fast-absorbing formulations sustains demand for light esters like this one across skin and hair care.

substitution.title: Other light C16-C18 esters
substitution.body: Interchangeable with several similar light emollient esters depending on specific sensory requirements.

functionalities.name: Multi-function emollient, UV filter solvent, and pigment wetter
functionalities.desc: A branched-chain fatty alcohol from Guerbet condensation of 2-ethylhexanol, used as an emollient, a solvent for crystalline UV filters, and a pigment-wetting agent in color cosmetics — genuinely multi-role, not single-purpose.

functionalities.name: Dominant feedstock is the same 2-EH used across the UV filter category
functionalities.desc: Directly ties this product's cost exposure to the same propylene/2-EH chain as octocrylene, ethylhexyl salicylate, and other UV filters already in this library.

items: Emollient, UV filter solvent, and pigment wetter in color cosmetics

tags: Major branched fatty alcohol emollient producer

OLE-ODD-LIQ.supplierNote: Octyldodecanol is a branched (Guerbet-type) fatty alcohol emollient — the Guerbet condensation step is more specialized than straight-chain fatty alcohol production, narrowing the producer base somewhat relative to the other esters in this cluster. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: No significant compliance or substitution concern identified
compliance.name: Synthetic Guerbet alcohol — no acute regulatory flag
compliance.desc: Made from petrochemical 2-ethylhexanol rather than a directly-regulated agricultural commodity; no EUDR exposure and no known material substitution threat.

macroDrivers.title: Color cosmetics pigment-wetting demand is a distinct driver from skin-care emollient demand
macroDrivers.body: This product's multi-role nature (emollient + UV filter solvent + pigment wetter) means its demand doesn't move in lockstep with any single personal-care subcategory.

substitution.title: Alpha-olefin oxo-route alternatives
substitution.body: An oxo-synthesis route from long-chain olefins offers a real alternative production pathway to the Guerbet route, though the finished product is functionally equivalent.

functionalities.name: Lightweight, fast-spreading silicone alternative
functionalities.desc: Transesterification of dimethyl carbonate with 2-ethylhexanol gives a very low-viscosity, silicone-mimicking sensory profile — increasingly replacing cyclomethicone (D5) as silicone-free formulation demand grows.

functionalities.name: Directly benefits from D5/cyclopentasiloxane's regulatory pressure
functionalities.desc: D5 faces EU REACH restrictions (wash-off since 2020, ongoing leave-on review) — this product is one of the primary beneficiaries of brand-side reformulation away from volatile silicones.

items: Silicone-alternative lightweight emollient in foundations, primers, and hair serums

OLE-DCC-LIQ.supplierNote: Dicaprylyl carbonate is specifically positioned as a silicone-alternative light-feel emollient, a smaller and more specialized niche than the broader emollient-ester category. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Beneficiary of D5/cyclomethicone regulatory restriction
compliance.name: Structural demand tailwind, not a restriction on this product itself
compliance.desc: This product carries no direct regulatory restriction — its growth is a direct consequence of restrictions on the silicone chemistry it's replacing.

macroDrivers.title: Silicone-free reformulation is a direct, quantifiable demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As D5/cyclopentasiloxane faces tightening EU restrictions, dicaprylyl carbonate is one of the clearest beneficiary substitutes — a structural, regulation-linked growth driver rather than a discretionary trend.

substitution.title: Other silicone-alternative esters (isododecane, C12-15 alkyl benzoate)
substitution.body: Competes with several other silicone-mimicking esters for the same reformulation demand — a real but crowded substitution space.

functionalities.name: Excellent UV filter solubilizer, used in nearly all sunscreen formulations
functionalities.desc: Esterification of benzoic acid with C12-C15 Ziegler alcohols gives an emollient specifically valued for its ability to dissolve and stabilize crystalline UV filters like avobenzone — a near-essential formulation component in sunscreen specifically, beyond its general emollient role.

functionalities.name: Directly tied to this library's existing UV filter cost chain
functionalities.desc: Its role as an avobenzone solubilizer means demand tracks sunscreen production volume closely, linking it functionally to F21-AVOB-PWD and the other UV filter products in this library.

items: UV filter solubilizer (especially avobenzone) — near-universal in sunscreen formulations
General light emollient

OLE-C1215AB-LIQ.supplierNote: C12-C15 alkyl benzoate is used specifically to solubilize UV filters in sunscreen formulations (overlapping with the F10/F21 sunscreen-actives clusters elsewhere in this library) — a narrower, more sunscreen-specific niche than the other general-purpose emollients in this cluster. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: No significant compliance or substitution concern identified
compliance.name: Synthetic emollient ester — no acute regulatory flag
compliance.desc: Built from benzoic acid and Ziegler-process synthetic alcohols rather than a directly-regulated agricultural commodity; no EUDR exposure identified.

macroDrivers.title: Sunscreen production volume is a direct demand driver given its near-universal solubilizer role
macroDrivers.body: Because this product is functionally required to stabilize avobenzone in most sunscreen formulations, its demand tracks sunscreen category volume very closely.

substitution.title: Other light ester solvents for avobenzone
substitution.body: A few alternative oil-soluble solvents can perform a similar avobenzone-stabilizing role, but this product's specific solvency profile keeps it the formulator default.

functionalities.name: The most common W/O emulsifier, classic Span/Tween system
functionalities.desc: Paired with Tween 60 (polysorbate) in the textbook water-in-oil emulsion system taught in every cosmetic formulation course — genuinely foundational, not a niche ingredient.

functionalities.name: Simplest possible ester model in this surfactant category
functionalities.desc: Straightforward esterification of sorbitol with stearic acid, both feedstocks already well-characterized elsewhere in this library.

items: W/O emulsifier, classic Span/Tween emulsion system component

tags: Span brand, paired with Tween (polysorbate) system

SUR-SMS-PWD.supplierNote: Sorbitan monostearate is the classic Span-series W/O emulsifier, almost always discussed alongside its Tween (polysorbate) HLB-balancing partner (see SUR-PS80-LIQ) — the two share much of the same producer base since both derive from sorbitol esterification chemistry. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) traceability
compliance.name: Stearic-acid feedstock is typically palm/tallow-derived
compliance.desc: Commercial stearic acid used in sorbitan monostearate is most often palm or animal-tallow derived; the palm-derived share falls under EUDR for EU-bound volumes.

macroDrivers.title: Fundamental emulsifier status ties demand to overall emulsion-based formulation volume
macroDrivers.body: As one of the most basic, widely-taught emulsifier chemistries, demand tracks broad personal care emulsion production.

substitution.title: Other sorbitan esters (Span 20, 80)
substitution.body: Different fatty acid chain lengths in the same sorbitan ester family serve slightly different HLB/emulsification needs.

functionalities.name: Bio-based, Ecocert-eligible emulsifier system
functionalities.desc: Fischer glycosidation of cetearyl alcohol with glucose gives a naturally-derived emulsifier increasingly required for 'natural cosmetics' certification — a real, growing certification-driven demand segment.

functionalities.name: Multi-branded across the same chemistry
functionalities.desc: Marketed under Montanov 68 (Syensqo/Novecare), Emulgade PL68/50 (BASF), and Fluidanov (Gattefossé) — the same core chemistry sold under several different brand names by different suppliers, worth knowing when comparing quotes.

items: Bio-based emulsifier for natural/organic-certified cosmetic formulations

SUR-CTG-PWD.supplierNote: Cetearyl glucoside is a bio-based, Ecocert/COSMOS-eligible emulsifier increasingly demanded for "natural cosmetics" certification — European specialty majors (BASF, Croda, Evonik, Seppic) with dedicated natural-ingredient lines lead this certification-driven segment, with Indian producers (Galaxy Surfactants) growing share on cost. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Ecocert/natural cosmetics certification eligibility
compliance.name: Certification-driving demand factor
compliance.desc: This ingredient's bio-based status is specifically relevant to Ecocert and similar natural-cosmetics certification requirements — a genuine certification-compliance driver, not just a marketing angle.

macroDrivers.title: Natural/organic cosmetics certification growth is a direct, structural demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As natural-cosmetics certification becomes more commercially important, bio-based emulsifiers like this one see durable, certification-linked demand growth.

substitution.title: Glyceryl stearate SE and other bio-based emulsifiers
substitution.body: Several other naturally-derived emulsifier systems compete for the same natural-certification-driven demand.

functionalities.name: Most widely used O/W emulsifier in skin care globally
functionalities.desc: Esterification of glycerine with stearic acid, plus a small potassium/sodium stearate soap addition for the self-emulsifying function — the standard workhorse emulsifier for oil-in-water creams and lotions.

functionalities.name: Simplest emulsifier model in this library
functionalities.desc: All feedstocks (glycerine, stearic acid, caustic) are basic, well-characterized commodity oleochemicals — one of the most straightforward cost models possible in the surfactant category.

items: Primary O/W self-emulsifying system in skin care creams and lotions globally

SUR-GSSE-PWD.supplierNote: Glyceryl stearate (self-emulsifying, with a small soap co-addition) is the single most widely used O/W emulsifier in skin care globally — essentially a commodity personal-care ingredient at this point, so the producer base is broad, spanning Western specialty majors and Asian oleochemical-integrated producers (Galaxy, KLK OLEO) with direct palm/coconut feedstock access. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) traceability
compliance.name: Palm-derived stearic acid and glycerine require deforestation-free evidence
compliance.desc: Both the stearic acid and glycerine inputs are typically palm-derived and fall under EUDR for EU-bound volumes.

macroDrivers.title: Universal O/W emulsifier status ties demand directly to overall skin care cream/lotion production
macroDrivers.body: As the default self-emulsifying system for O/W formulations, demand growth tracks total skin care production volume closely.

substitution.title: Cetearyl glucoside and other bio-based emulsifiers
substitution.body: For natural-certified formulations specifically, bio-based alternatives substitute — otherwise this remains the default low-cost choice.

functionalities.name: Premium non-ionic emulsifier for natural/organic cosmetics
functionalities.desc: Esterification of polyglycerol-4 (from alkaline thermal glycerine polymerization) with lauric acid gives a premium emulsifier well-suited to natural formulation positioning.

functionalities.name: Part of a broader polyglycerol ester family with varied chain lengths
functionalities.desc: Different polyglycerol esters (varying both the glycerol oligomer length and fatty acid chain) offer a tunable HLB range for different emulsification needs.

items: Premium non-ionic emulsifier, especially in natural/organic-positioned cosmetics

tags: Polyglycerol ester specialist — Novecare personal-care emulsifier business, moved to Syensqo in the Dec 2023 Solvay/Syensqo demerger, not the remaining Solvay entity

SUR-PGL4-LIQ.supplierNote: Polyglyceryl-4 laurate is a premium, natural-formulation-positioned non-ionic emulsifier with a more concentrated producer base than commodity emulsifiers — the polyglycerol synthesis step (alkaline thermal glycerine polymerization) is a more specialized process than simple fatty-acid esterification. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Sourcing-dependent EUDR exposure
compliance.name: Lauric acid (coconut) is not currently EUDR-covered; glycerine may be
compliance.desc: Coconut-derived lauric acid is not one of the seven commodities currently covered by the EU Deforestation Regulation, so this input carries no EUDR exposure; however, if the glycerine input is palm-derived rather than synthetic, that portion would still be in scope.

macroDrivers.title: Natural/organic cosmetics positioning is the primary demand driver
macroDrivers.body: This product's premium positioning ties its growth closely to the natural/organic cosmetics segment specifically, more than mass-market skin care generally.

substitution.title: Cetearyl glucoside and other natural-positioned emulsifiers
substitution.body: Competes with several other natural-certification-eligible emulsifiers for the same premium formulation segment.

functionalities.name: Dominant cationic conditioning agent for hair conditioners and treatments
functionalities.desc: Quaternization of behenyl amine (from behenic acid/rapeseed oil) with methyl chloride gives the longest-chain (C22), highest-conditioning-power quaternary ammonium compound in common commercial use — offers more lubricity and conditioning than the shorter-chain cetrimonium chloride.

functionalities.name: Directly derived from this library's existing C20-C22 behenyl fatty alcohol chain
functionalities.desc: The behenyl amine input is a direct downstream derivative of the OLE-FAL-C20 behenyl fatty alcohol already modeled in this library.

items: Primary cationic conditioning agent in hair conditioners, treatments, and leave-in products

SUR-BTAC-PST.supplierNote: Behentrimonium chloride is the premium, longest-chain (C22) quat conditioning agent, commanding a price premium over the more commodity CTAC (see SUR-CTAC-LIQ) — producer base overlaps heavily with CTAC since both are quaternization products, differing mainly in feedstock fatty amine chain length. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Rapeseed oil feedstock sourcing (high-erucic variety specifically)
compliance.name: Feedstock-specific sourcing note
compliance.desc: Behenic acid derives specifically from high-erucic rapeseed oil, a distinct agricultural variety from standard canola — relevant context for feedstock availability discussions.

macroDrivers.title: Premium hair conditioning/treatment segment growth is the primary demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As the highest-conditioning-power common quat, BTAC benefits disproportionately from premium hair care segment growth versus basic rinse-off conditioners.

substitution.title: Cetrimonium chloride (shorter C16 chain)
substitution.body: CTAC offers lower conditioning power at lower cost — a real but performance-differentiated substitution, not a direct equivalent swap.

functionalities.name: Most common cationic surfactant for rinse-off hair conditioning
functionalities.desc: Quaternization of cetyl amine with methyl chloride gives the standard, highest-volume cationic conditioning surfactant for everyday rinse-off conditioners — the commodity end of the quat category versus BTAC's premium positioning.

functionalities.name: Straightforward, fully-indexed feedstock chain
functionalities.desc: Fatty alcohol, ammonia, methanol, and HCl are all well-characterized in this library — one of the cleaner cost models in the cationic surfactant category.

items: Standard cationic conditioning surfactant in everyday rinse-off hair conditioning products

SUR-CTAC-LIQ.supplierNote: CTAC is the highest-volume, most commodity-end cationic conditioning surfactant, used in everyday rinse-off conditioners — this is a more price-competitive, higher-volume market than the premium BTAC (see SUR-BTAC-PST), with Chinese producers (Zanyu, Guangzhou Tinci) competing more directly on cost at this commodity end. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Mild reformulation pressure toward readily-biodegradable ester-quats
compliance.name: Structural formulation consideration, not an acute risk
compliance.desc: Conventional quaternary ammonium conditioning agents like CTAC have faced gradual reformulation pressure in some markets toward more readily biodegradable ester-quat alternatives, echoing the broader 1990s-2000s shift away from persistent fabric-softener quats; CTAC remains a widely used, cost-effective commodity-grade conditioning agent in hair care.

macroDrivers.title: Mass-market rinse-off conditioner volume is the core demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As the standard commodity quat, CTAC demand tracks total rinse-off hair conditioner production volume directly.

substitution.title: Behentrimonium chloride for premium positioning
substitution.body: Formulators upgrade to BTAC for premium/treatment products requiring higher conditioning power, at a cost premium.

functionalities.name: Mild anionic with excellent foaming, used in sulfate-free shampoos and toothpaste
functionalities.desc: Acylation of sodium sarcosinate (from methylglycine) with lauroyl chloride gives a mild anionic surfactant valued specifically for combining good foam with low irritation — used across sulfate-free shampoos, toothpaste, and facial cleansers.

functionalities.name: Toothpaste application is a distinct, non-personal-care-cosmetic demand pool
functionalities.desc: Its use in toothpaste formulations ties part of its demand to oral care volume specifically, distinct from shampoo/cleanser demand cycles.

items: Mild anionic surfactant in sulfate-free shampoos and facial cleansers
Foaming agent in toothpaste formulations

SUR-SLSAR-LIQ.supplierNote: Sodium lauroyl sarcosinate is a mild anionic surfactant used in sulfate-free shampoos and toothpaste — amino-acid-based surfactants are a more specialized niche than sulfate/sulfonate surfactants, with Japanese producers (Kawaken) historically strong in this specific amino-acid surfactant category. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: No significant compliance or substitution concern identified
compliance.name: Coconut-derived mild anionic — no acute regulatory flag
compliance.desc: Built from coconut-derived lauric acid, which is not an EUDR-covered commodity; sodium lauroyl sarcosinate is well-established as a mild, biodegradable surfactant with no known material substitution threat.

macroDrivers.title: Dual personal care and oral care demand base provides genuine diversification
macroDrivers.body: Unlike most surfactants in this category tied purely to shampoo/cleanser cycles, this product's toothpaste application adds a distinct, more stable oral-care demand layer.

substitution.title: Sodium cocoyl isethionate and other mild anionics
substitution.body: Competes with several other mild anionic surfactants for sulfate-free reformulation demand specifically in shampoo/cleanser applications (not toothpaste, where its role is more entrenched).

functionalities.name: Most widely used cationic conditioning polymer in shampoos and conditioners globally
functionalities.desc: Quaternization of hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC) with glycidyltrimethylammonium chloride (GTAC) gives a cationic polymer that deposits on hair and skin for conditioning — the standard conditioning-polymer technology across the mass-market hair care industry.

functionalities.name: Direct derivative of this library's existing HEC model
functionalities.desc: Built on the HEC backbone already modeled in this library (F24-HEC-EU) — this product's cost structure is best understood as that existing model plus a quaternization conversion step.

items: Standard cationic conditioning polymer in mass-market shampoos and conditioners globally

tags: China Asia challenger — named individual Chinese cellulose-ether producer, same HEADCEL business referenced elsewhere in this library for HPMC

F24-PQ10-PWD.supplierNote: Dow's Ucare Polymer JR line is the long-standing category reference; given that HEC itself (the polymer backbone) has substantial Chinese production capacity, a real generic Chinese quaternized-HEC supply chain has developed downstream as well, though branded Western material remains dominant for premium mass-market formulations requiring documented, consistent deposition performance.

compliance.flag: No significant compliance or substitution concern identified
compliance.name: Established cationic cellulose conditioning polymer — no acute regulatory flag
compliance.desc: Polyquaternium-10 is a widely used, established cosmetic ingredient with no known compliance concern.

macroDrivers.title: Mass-market shampoo/conditioner volume is the core, direct demand driver
macroDrivers.body: As the standard conditioning-polymer technology for mass-market hair care, demand tracks total global shampoo/conditioner production volume very directly.

substitution.title: Guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride (GHPTC)
substitution.body: A bio-based cationic conditioning polymer already in this library (F24-GHPTC-PWD) competes directly for the same conditioning-polymer role, particularly in natural-positioned formulations — a genuine, not theoretical, substitution option.

functionalities.name: Dominant beta-hydroxy acid (BHA) for acne treatment and exfoliation
functionalities.desc: Made via the classic Kolbe-Schmitt reaction (sodium phenolate + CO2 under pressure) — well-documented, standard industrial chemistry with predictable stoichiometry, giving this one of the cleanest cost models among personal care actives.

functionalities.name: Also a direct feedstock for the UV filter category in this library
functionalities.desc: Salicylic acid is itself the direct precursor for ethylhexyl salicylate and homosalate, both already modeled in this library — this product sits directly upstream of two existing UV filter cost chains.

items: Primary BHA exfoliant and acne-treatment active in cleansers, toners, and spot treatments

tags: Major dedicated salicylic acid/salicylate derivatives producer
China Asia challenger — dominant named Chinese producer

F23-SALAC-PWD.supplierNote: Croda, BASF, and Clariant all use this as a formulation active in their skin care actives portfolios but are not primary producers themselves — the actual production base is more specialized (Novacyl, Siddharth Carbochem) plus a significant Chinese generic manufacturing base, since the underlying Kolbe-Schmitt chemistry is standard, well-documented industrial process with no major technical barrier.

compliance.flag: Cosmetic-grade vs. pharmaceutical-grade (aspirin precursor) distinction
compliance.name: Same molecule, different grade requirements
compliance.desc: Salicylic acid is also the direct precursor to aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) — pharmaceutical-grade material requires distinct purity documentation from cosmetic-grade; confirm grade matches intended use.

macroDrivers.title: Acne treatment and exfoliation category growth is the core demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Sustained consumer interest in BHA-based exfoliation and acne treatment provides steady, broad-based demand across skin care price tiers.

substitution.title: Glycolic acid and other AHAs for exfoliation specifically
substitution.body: For general exfoliation (not acne-specific treatment), alpha-hydroxy acids like glycolic acid can substitute — but salicylic acid's specific pore-penetrating, oil-soluble property for acne treatment has no direct AHA equivalent.

functionalities.name: Most popular alpha-hydroxy acid for skin peels and anti-aging
functionalities.desc: Two commercially viable synthesis routes exist — formaldehyde+CO+water (the DuPont/Chemours process) or chloroacetic acid hydrolysis — giving genuine route flexibility depending on regional feedstock economics.

functionalities.name: Dual production route gives real regional cost-optimization flexibility
functionalities.desc: North American production tends to favor the natural-gas-linked CO route; regions with cheaper chlor-alkali economics may favor the chloroacetic acid route — both produce an identical finished product.

items: Leading AHA for chemical peels, anti-aging, and general exfoliation across all major personal care actives portfolios

tags: Originator of the formaldehyde+CO synthesis route
Named individual European producer — Gersthofen, Bavaria integrated chlorine-electrolysis plant produces glycolic acid alongside other chloroacetic-acid-chain specialties

F23-GLYAC-LIQ.supplierNote: Used by all major personal care companies as a formulation active but produced by a distinct, more specialized set of chemical manufacturers (Chemours, CrossChem, Zhonglan) rather than the Croda/BASF/Evonik/Clariant emollient-and-surfactant majors — worth keeping this producer set distinct from the rest of this personal care batch when evaluating supplier consolidation opportunities.

compliance.flag: Route-dependent chlorine/chloroacetic acid residual specification
compliance.name: Route-specific quality consideration
compliance.desc: Material produced via the chloroacetic acid route requires verification of residual chlorinated byproduct levels — a genuine quality-control distinction between the two production routes, not merely a sourcing preference.

macroDrivers.title: Chemical peel and anti-aging category growth is the core structural demand driver
macroDrivers.body: Sustained, broad consumer interest in AHA-based anti-aging and resurfacing treatments provides durable demand across professional and at-home skin care segments.

substitution.title: Lactic acid and other AHAs
substitution.body: Other alpha-hydroxy acids (lactic, mandelic) substitute for gentler or specific-skin-type formulations — a real but performance-differentiated substitution space, not a like-for-like swap.

functionalities.name: The foundational aromatic — feeds an enormous share of this entire library
functionalities.desc: Extracted from naphtha reformate/pyrolysis gasoline (BTX extraction) at refinery aromatics complexes — benzene is the direct or indirect feedstock for dozens of products already in this database (styrene, phenol, cyclohexane, UV filters, surfactant intermediates, and more) via the BZ-EU/NA/CN/ASIA indexes referenced throughout.

functionalities.name: Genuinely commodity, tight-margin, refinery-integrated product
functionalities.desc: Benzene contract prices are themselves published, liquid indexes (ICIS, Platts) — this product card is essentially a thin margin wrapper on a price the market already discovers directly, not a complex proprietary formulation.

items: Foundational feedstock for styrene, phenol, cyclohexane, cumene, and nitrobenzene — the starting point for a vast downstream aromatic chemistry tree
Foundational aromatic feedstock for polystyrene, ABS, nylon, and polycarbonate resin chains

China Asia challenger — integrated refining, growing aromatics capacity
Verbund integration incl. Zhanjiang, China cracker-styrene complex
Asia challenger — Jamnagar integrated refinery-aromatics complex
Asia challenger — Korean aromatics majors, though under margin pressure in 2025-2026

BCI-BENZ-LIQ.supplierNote: Benzene is produced almost exclusively as a byproduct of refinery reforming and steam-cracker pygas extraction, so supply is tied to each producer’s refinery/cracker economics rather than dedicated benzene capacity decisions. China (Sinopec, PetroChina, plus private integrators like Hengli and Rongsheng) has become the largest single producing and consuming region, with Asia-Pacific accounting for roughly 70%+ of global demand. Exact tonnage market shares are not consistently disclosed at the company level; treat share:0 as “not disclosed,” not “zero volume.”

compliance.flag: Known human carcinogen (Group 1, IARC)
compliance.name: Severe, well-established health hazard
compliance.desc: Benzene is a confirmed human carcinogen with strict occupational exposure limits globally — transport, storage, and handling carry significant regulatory documentation requirements independent of any specific formulation use.

macroDrivers.title: Refinery/cracker utilization and naphtha spread are the dominant structural price drivers
macroDrivers.body: Because benzene is fundamentally a refinery/cracker byproduct, its price is more exposed to naphtha cracking economics and aromatics complex utilization rates than to benzene-specific demand alone.

substitution.title: No meaningful substitute — foundational, irreplaceable aromatic
substitution.desc: As the entry point to an enormous downstream chemistry tree, benzene has no practical substitute; the only real lever is sourcing from different regional aromatics complexes.

functionalities.name: Key intermediate for MEG, ethoxylates, and ethanolamines
functionalities.desc: Direct oxidation of ethylene with a silver catalyst gives an extremely reactive gas/liquid that is itself the feedstock for MEG (already in this library), a wide range of surfactant ethoxylates, and ethanolamines.

functionalities.name: Widely referenced throughout this library but never modeled as its own product until now
functionalities.desc: The EO-EU/EO-ASIA index type-codes appear across dozens of formulas in this database (surfactants, glycols, amines) — this card closes that structural gap.

items: Feedstock for monoethylene glycol (MEG), ethoxylated surfactants, ethanolamines, and polyethylene glycol
Ethoxylation feedstock for SLES, ethoxylated emollients, and PEG derivatives used across personal care
Ethoxylation feedstock for non-ionic surfactants, SLES, and AES in household and I&I detergents

BCI-EO-LIQ.supplierNote: EO is an extremely hazardous, highly reactive gas almost always produced and consumed on an integrated, co-located basis (EO plant feeding a downstream MEG/ethoxylate/ethanolamine unit on the same site), so it is rarely traded as a standalone merchant commodity. Asia-Pacific holds roughly 55% of global production, with China alone approaching 70% of regional output; new Chinese capacity (Yulong, Wanhua, and others) is adding disproportionately to global supply. Exact company-level shares are not consistently disclosed; treat share:0 as “not disclosed.”

compliance.flag: Extremely reactive, flammable, and carcinogenic gas
compliance.name: Severe handling/transport hazard, integrated-production norm
compliance.desc: EO's extreme reactivity and toxicity mean it is rarely transported far from its production site — most commercial supply chains are built around integrated on-site downstream conversion rather than merchant EO shipment.

macroDrivers.title: Ethylene/naphtha cracking economics are the dominant cost driver
macroDrivers.body: As a direct ethylene derivative, EO cost tracks ethylene/naphtha cracker economics closely — the same driver affecting MEG and other ethylene derivatives in this library.

substitution.title: No practical substitute for its specific downstream chemistry roles
substitution.desc: MEG, ethoxylates, and ethanolamines each depend specifically on EO's epoxide reactivity — no broad substitute exists at the intermediate level.

functionalities.name: Feedstock for ABS, acrylic fibers, and nitrile rubber
functionalities.desc: Made via Sohio ammoxidation of propylene with ammonia and oxygen — feeds this library's existing ABS (RES-ABS-PEL) and NBR (ELA-NBR-BAL) products directly, plus acrylic fiber production.

functionalities.name: Genuinely topical: real recent regional capacity exit
functionalities.desc: PTT Asahi Chemical (a GC-linked JV) ceased AN operations in January 2025 — GC's downstream ABS/NBR businesses now import AN rather than produce it domestically, a real, recent, verifiable supply-chain shift.

items: Feedstock for ABS resin, acrylic fibers, nitrile rubber (NBR), and adiponitrile (nylon 6,6 precursor)
ABS resin, acrylic fiber, and NBR rubber comonomer

Acrylamide and polyacrylamide flocculant monomer feedstock
